ReductiveGroupsPartII.title: Reductive algebraic groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models
ReductiveGroupsPartII.reason: Use the exact anchor title and put the anchor first among prerequisites. Retain the seven RG2 stages; valued roots, buildings, connected parahoric models, local decompositions, affine Weil restriction and the functorial integral dual interface extend the existing algebraic theory.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0.reason: Retain all point-topology constructions, chart-independence, functoriality, separated finite-type local compactness/Hausdorffness, group continuity, integral compactness and congruence-neighbourhood results. Use the upstream functor-of-points/group-scheme dictionary and specialize the pinned GeneralLinear points equivalence for the GL_n acceptance test; the new topology/comparison is not supplied by that algebraic equivalence.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0a.reason: Retain affine finite-type Weil restriction along finite locally free maps, representing algebra, finite-presentation theorem under its stated hypothesis, adjunction/evaluation, products/composition/base change and coherence, finite-separable splitting/descent, Deligne torus with norm/weight maps, and every listed example. Import the existing group-scheme and torus carriers. Neither abstract tori nor module restriction of scalars constructs this representing scheme. Do not generalize to arbitrary nonaffine schemes or inseparable reductivity.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1.keeps: Import the algebraic relative roots and relative Weyl group of a maximal E-split torus, and the absolute root datum/Galois-action and parabolic structure from anchor Layer 7. Retain the local-field realization and comparison of the root groups, their valuation filtrations at their actual valuation sets, the nonsplit and multipliable-root cases, valued commutator estimates, torus conjugation and unramified-extension compatibility. Construct the affine root functions and apartment from this valued datum, with transport under choices. Do not reconstruct the underlying unvalued relative-root theory.
ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.1.reason: Anchor Layer 7 explicitly owns relative root systems for nonsplit groups as well as split/absolute data. RG2.1 owns the valued enhancement and affine apartment; the word relative alone does not distinguish its scope.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2.reason: Retain apartment gluing, transition maps, building axioms, G(E)-action, pair-of-points apartment existence, reduced/enlarged comparison and parametrization independence, facets/closure/fixers, compactness modulo center and the bounded-subgroup fixed-point theorem with hypotheses. Retain the GL_n norm/lattice-chain model and SL_2 tree. An algebraic root datum or BN-pair does not supply these geometric constructions.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3.reason: Retain construction of the connected smooth affine Bruhat–Tits O_E-model, root charts, generic fiber and integral-point characterization, its special-fiber reductive quotient and reduction/pro-unipotent data, pro-p congruence groups and compact openness, nested-facet maps and unramified base change. Keep the map to the fixer model and component comparison, and the distinction from hyperspecial models. Use anchor group-scheme, quotient, unipotent-radical and reductivity notions: a supplied predicate is not a construction or proof of reductivity of this particular quotient.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4.keeps: Retain nonarchimedean Iwasawa decomposition with an appropriate special maximal compact, Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their precise field/group ranges, local Tits-system construction where applicable, and all relative-cocharacter, affine/extended-Weyl, dominance, stabilizer and component identifications. Import abstract algebraic Bruhat/BN-pair theory from Layer 7 and the existing pinned abstract Tits-system covering theorem, proving its hypotheses for the local subgroup to which it is applied. Handle any larger ambient group/component cosets explicitly; do not assume an ordinary affine BN-pair covers every G(E). Keep compact-open double-coset index formulas and finiteness of the single-coset decomposition of each compact double coset, with rank-one and nonsplit examples. This is not a claim that the entire Cartan double-coset set is finite.
ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4.reason: The anchor owns abstract Bruhat and BN-pair theory, but does not construct the local valued subgroups or prove Iwasawa/Cartan decompositions for nonarchimedean points. The local identifications and hypotheses remain new work.

ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5.keeps: Use anchor Layer 7 to extract the absolute based root datum and its Galois action from the E-form. Dualize using the existing root-pairing flip and apply anchor Layer 9’s explicit pinned Chevalley–Demazure construction to obtain the integral dual, rather than rebuilding a general pinned split group. Retain the identification of its datum with the dual one, the continuous finite-image pinning action, the semidirect L-group with projection/action law, change-of-pinning equivalences, Levi inclusions and compatibility with products, central isogenies and RG2.0a Weil restriction. Retain split-torus and GL_n tests. Parameter spaces remain LanglandsParameterStacks; coefficient square roots and geometric/pinned Satake-action comparisons remain in their consuming Satake stages.
ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5.reason: The generic pinned split group construction and uniqueness are anchor Layer 9 work. The dualization application, induced action and functorial L-group interface are RG2.5 work, required independently of Tannakian Satake reconstruction.
